text: Instead of calf rennet or acid, a plant enzyme clots the milk. Which plant decides the cheese: cardoon in Iberian ewe's-milk cheeses, Calotropis in West African wagashi, papaya in Indonesian dangke. The enzyme of Calotropis procera sets the milk but breaks protein down little, so the cheese can be reboiled every other day and kept for about a month (Licitra, quoted in Seini et al. 2018).
